final_answer:
Short answer: No. On these facts Client very likely cannot lawfully stop paying Lessor, and Lessor is not responsible for the defective Trailers. Client's remedy lies against Manufacturer (now in Chapter 7), not Lessor. Caveat: I could not retrieve the Virginia Code text directly (egress blocked); the statutory points below rest on search-result excerpts of Va. Code Title 8.2A, which enacts uniform UCC Article 2A, and on the uniform Official Comments. Section numbers should be cite-checked, and I found no Virginia case on point.

1. The deal is a 'finance lease' under Va. Code 8.2A-103(1)(g). The definition requires that (i) the lessor does not select, manufacture, or supply the goods; (ii) the lessor acquires the goods in connection with the lease; and (iii) one of three things occurs: the lessee receives a copy of the supply contract before signing the lease; the lessee's approval of the supply contract is a condition to the lease's effectiveness; or, before signing, the lessee receives an accurate and complete statement of the supplier's promises, warranties, disclaimers and remedy limitations. Here Client chose the model and negotiated the refrigeration specs with Manufacturer, Lessor merely bought and financed the Trailers, and Lessor gave Client a complete copy of the purchase agreement (with the two-year warranty) before Client signed. All elements are met. Client's selection of the goods is what makes Lessor a financier rather than a 'supplier'. The lease is a commercial one, not a consumer lease.

2. Hell-or-high-water. Under 8.2A-407, in a finance lease that is not a consumer lease, the lessee's promises become irrevocable and independent upon acceptance of the goods. They are enforceable between the parties and by or against assignees and are not subject to cancellation, termination, modification, repudiation, excuse or substitution without the consent of the party to whom the promise runs. The section is self-executing, and the Lease's 'absolute and unconditional, irrespective of any defense or setoff, counterclaim or recoupment' clause independently confirms the result. The Official Comment says the lessee may not stop paying rent or set off its damages against rent, although it may have a damages claim for the lessor's own breach and a claim against the supplier. Client accepted and used the Trailers for four months, so its rent obligations became irrevocable. The compressor failures arose after acceptance and do not excuse payment. Because the Lease and the statute both bar setoff, Client cannot withhold rent to offset warranty losses.

3. Revocation of acceptance. Acceptance of finance-leased goods generally cannot be revoked against the lessor for supplier defects, and the Comment to 8.2A-407 notes that acceptance made with knowledge of a nonconformity is not revocable. Under 8.2A-517 revocation requires a substantial impairment that was latent or that acceptance was induced by assurances. Even if Client could satisfy that, the finance-lease structure routes the remedy to the supplier. I could not verify the exact Virginia text of 8.2A-516/517 and flag that as a point to check.

4. Lessor's responsibility for the defects. In a finance lease the lessor gives no implied warranty of merchantability or fitness (8.2A-212, 8.2A-213 do not apply to finance leases). Lessor does give only the limited warranties against interference and infringement (8.2A-211). The Lease also disclaims Lessor warranties and directs equipment claims to Manufacturer. Under 8.2A-209, the supplier's promises and warranties to the lessor under the supply contract, including Manufacturer's two-year warranty on mechanical and refrigeration components, extend to the lessee as beneficiary, and the existence of those warranties does not make the lessor liable for them. The risk of supplier non-performance, including supplier insolvency, therefore falls on the lessee. This is the bargain a finance lease allocates: the lessee gets the supplier's warranties instead of lessor warranties.

5. Consequences and options. If Client stops paying, it is in default under 8.2A-501 et seq., and Lessor may exercise remedies such as accelerating rent, repossessing and re-leasing or selling the Trailers, and recovering the unpaid rent and damages under Article 2A Part 5 Article C (8.2A-523 to 8.2A-529), plus any contractual remedies (late charges, attorney's fees, guaranties). The remaining rent obligation is about $2,200 x 2 x 56 months, about $246,000, before discounting. Client should keep paying under reservation of rights and pursue: (a) a proof of claim in Manufacturer's Chapter 7 for breach of warranty (likely an unsecured claim with little recovery); (b) any extended or component warranty from the compressor maker, or a third-party/insurance warranty; (c) repair at Client's own expense; (d) negotiation with Lessor for a voluntary restructure or substitution. Client may also check whether the trustee's refusal to perform leaves any assignable warranty rights against the compressor component supplier.

6. Possible exceptions to check. Lessor could be liable only for its own breach, such as misrepresentation about the Trailers, fraud, or its own breach of the Lease. Unconscionability (8.2A-108) is unlikely between commercial parties with a lessee that had a full copy of the supply contract. A Lessor that actually selected, manufactured or supplied the goods would not be a finance lessor, but Client selected here. Facts to verify: any Lessor representations about the Trailers, whether Lessor's purchase agreement terms were fully and accurately disclosed, whether the Lease assigns warranty rights to Client, and whether Lessor has assigned the Lease to a third party.

issues.text: Does the transaction qualify as a finance lease under Va. Code 8.2A-103(1)(g)?
Do 8.2A-407 and the hell-or-high-water clause make Client's rent obligation irrevocable and independent, barring withholding or setoff for supplier warranty failure?
Is Lessor liable for Manufacturer's defects given no lessor warranties and 8.2A-209 benefit of supplier's warranties?
Can Client revoke acceptance or otherwise excuse performance, and what are the consequences of default and Client's remaining remedies against Manufacturer's bankruptcy estate?
Are there exceptions (lessor's own misconduct, unconscionability, nonconsumer status)?

authorities.title: Definitions: finance lease
authorities.proposition: A finance lease is one where the lessor does not select, manufacture or supply the goods, acquires them in connection with the lease, and the lessee receives the supply contract or an accurate and complete statement of supplier warranties before signing.

authorities.title: Irrevocable promises: finance leases
authorities.proposition: In a non-consumer finance lease the lessee's promises become irrevocable and independent upon acceptance; the lessee may not stop paying rent or set off; the lessee's remedy is against the supplier.

authorities.title: Lessee under finance lease as beneficiary of supply contract
authorities.proposition: Supplier's promises and warranties extend to the finance lessee, and the lessor is not thereby made liable for them.

authorities.title: Lessor warranties, revocation, default remedies
authorities.proposition: Implied warranties of merchantability and fitness do not arise from a finance lessor; lessor has remedies on lessee default.

authorities.title: Uniform text and comment for irrevocable promises: finance leases
authorities.proposition: Self-executing hell-or-high-water; lessee may not stop paying or set off, may have a claim against the supplier; acceptance with knowledge of nonconformity is not revocable.

claims.text: The transaction is a finance lease because Client selected the Trailers and negotiated specs with Manufacturer, Lessor only acquired and financed them, and Client received a complete copy of the supply contract before signing.
Upon acceptance, Client's rent promises are irrevocable and independent under 8.2A-407 and the Lease clause, so Client cannot stop paying or set off for the compressor failures.

Lessor gave no warranties and is not liable for Manufacturer's defects or insolvency; Client holds the benefit of Manufacturer's warranty under 8.2A-209 and its recourse is against Manufacturer's estate.
Stopping payment is a default exposing Client to Lessor's Article 2A remedies, including accelerated rent and repossession.
